version.changelog: Prefer the bundled Search1API MCP tools, add browser-based CLI login and self-update guidance, document fetch-by-result-ID workflows, and remove the retired reasoning command.

llm.summary: This web-search skill is mostly purpose-aligned, but its install instructions and data-sharing defaults need human review before use.

dimensions.detail: External transmission of search terms and URLs is inherent to the service, but the artifact does not scope or limit sensitive data submission; sitemap and crawl workflows can expose full URLs and site structure to a third party.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: If no transport is available, the skill suggests a remote installer executed directly by bash and an unpinned global npm install; both are avoidable high-impact supply-chain risks even though installation is user-directed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill triggers on broad lookup language and bare URLs, then instructs crawling or searching through Search1API without a clear user-facing privacy warning or confirmation step for sensitive queries, private URLs, signed links, or internal hosts.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The global CLI install, s1 update path, browser login, manual API-key configuration, and SEARCH1API_KEY option create persistent local tooling or credentials, but the artifact provides little guidance on version pinning, credential safety, or what the installer changes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is live web search, page retrieval, news, sitemap discovery, trending topics, and balance checks through Search1API MCP tools or the s1 CLI; those capabilities fit the skill's purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Prefer the connected MCP tool or a verified, pinned CLI installation over the curl-to-bash or unpinned global npm commands. Do not submit secrets, signed URLs, private/internal links, regulated data, or confidential research terms unless you are comfortable sending them to Search1API and any selected search provider. Use browser login rather than pasting API keys where possible, and keep keys out of chat, logs, and shell history.
llm.findings:
[SC2] unexpected: The artifact does include curl -fsSL https://cli.search1api.com/install.sh | bash. Installing a CLI is purpose-related, but executing an unverified remote script directly is not necessary or proportionate.
[TM2] unexpected: The pipe-to-bash pattern is confirmed in SKILL.md and compounds the installer concern; there is no instruction to inspect, verify, pin, or otherwise constrain the downloaded script.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending queries and URLs to Search1API is expected for web search and crawling, but the artifact does not warn users or require confirmation before sending potentially sensitive URLs or research terms.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad search and URL triggers fit a web-search skill, but the bare-URL trigger is under-scoped because it can route sensitive links to an external crawler without an explicit sensitivity check.
[SQP-3] expected: The examples tell agents to use Baidu for Chinese queries, while the main SKILL.md gives different Chinese-engine guidance; this is a lower-impact routing and disclosure concern rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[T03] unexpected: The static finding is supported by the same remote installer command in SKILL.md; this justifies Review but not malicious classification because the artifact discloses the command and does not instruct hidden execution.
[T08] unexpected: The npm install -g search1api-cli instruction is confirmed and unpinned; it is a supply-chain and persistence concern, but it is an alternate user-directed install path for the stated CLI.
[T09] expected: The external submission concern is supported by the search, news, crawl, sitemap, and bare-URL workflows; no artifact evidence shows intentional API-key exfiltration or hidden local data collection.
